business: A salon's own staff-and-owner phone app (billing, walk-ins, wallet, WhatsApp reminders, attendance, live floor), set up per salon
target: Owners of small independent hair and beauty salons in Indian cities (1 to 8 chairs) who keep billing and customer details in a register, a notebook or WhatsApp today

segments.name: One-chair or two-chair men's salon or barber shop, owner also cuts hair
Neighbourhood unisex salon or ladies' parlour with 2 to 4 chairs and 2 to 4 staff
Established salon with 5 to 8 chairs and 5 to 10 staff
Premium or franchise salon outlet owner, sometimes 2 outlets

behaviours.name: Paper register loyalist
behaviours.how: Has written every bill in a register for years and trusts it more than any app.

behaviours.name: Runs everything on WhatsApp
behaviours.how: Customers, staff groups and bookings all live in WhatsApp chats on one phone.

behaviours.name: Counts every rupee
behaviours.how: Compares prices, asks for discounts, avoids monthly subscriptions.

behaviours.name: Tried an app before and stopped
behaviours.how: Paid for salon software once; the staff never used it and it was cancelled.

behaviours.name: Owner who isn't always at the salon
behaviours.how: Has another job or a second outlet and worries about cash and staff when away.

behaviours.name: Asks other owners first
behaviours.how: Buys only what a product distributor or another salon owner already uses.

behaviours.name: Young owner who likes tech
behaviours.how: Uses UPI, Instagram and Google reviews; looks for tools that make the salon look modern.

objections: ₹999 a month is one more fixed cost, and some months are slow
My staff are busy with customers; they won't type everything into an app
I already use a billing app or Zylu/MioSalon, why switch
What if the phone breaks and I lose all my customer data?
A selfie check-in will make my staff feel I don't trust them
Many of my customers won't give their mobile number
I want it in Hindi or my own language, not only English
Who will help me when something stops working on a busy Sunday?
habits: Sundays and festival weeks are your busiest days
you count the cash drawer yourself every night
you get product supplies from a local distributor who visits monthly
your customers mostly pay by UPI now
you lost two good stylists to a nearby salon last year
you post before-and-after photos on Instagram some weeks
